papers.title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Visual Servo Control with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
papers.abstract: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Franka Emika Panda robot arm, despite an imprecise digital twin, measurement errors, and noise. Our novel approach augments a loop-shaped inverse-Jacobian PI controller with a residual policy learned via Soft Actor-Critic in the digital twin. A delay-compensated Kalman filter fuses out-of-sequence camera measurements to provide latency-aware moving target position estimates. We compare the achieved performance to a performance bound for a class of model-based controllers derived from a frequency-domain sensitivity analysis, quantifying the minimum achievable error imposed by uncertain kinematic model mismatch. Simulation and hardware experiments indicate that our residual policy drives tracking error below the bound. Across conveyor speeds (27.9-41.8 mm/s), our method reduces mean tracking errors from 1.1-1.4 mm (baseline inverse-Jacobian PI) to 0.3-0.7 mm. These results show that learning residual corrections in a limited-fidelity simulator, combined with delay compensation, can substantially improve model-based control under modeling and measurement uncertainties while maintaining reliable sim-to-real transfer.
papers.headline: 学習した補正と遅延対策で、コンベヤ上の物体を高精度に追うロボット制御
papers.summary: コンベヤ上の移動物体をロボットアームで追う際の、モデルのずれや観測遅延による誤差を抑える研究です。従来の制御器にシミュレーションで学んだ補正を加え、カメラ観測の遅延も補償します。シミュレーションと実機で検証し、平均追従誤差の低減を報告しています。
papers.advantages: モデルに基づく制御を置き換えず、強化学習による補正を加える点が特徴です。著者らは、不完全なシミュレータでも有効な補正を学べると主張しています。比較実験では、補正前の制御器より平均追従誤差が小さくなりました。また、特定のモデルベース制御器群について導いた誤差の下限も下回ったと報告しています。あらゆる制御方式の限界を超えたという意味ではありません。
papers.method: カメラから届く、取得順と到着順が異なる観測を、遅延補償付きカルマンフィルタで統合します。これにより移動物体の位置を遅延を考慮して推定します。位置誤差に応じて動くPI制御と、手先の動きを関節の動きへ変換する逆ヤコビアンに、学習済みの補正を追加します。補正は実機を模したシミュレータ内で、強化学習手法Soft Actor-Criticを使って学びます。
papers.evaluation: Franka Emika Pandaアームによるコンベヤ上の移動物体の追従を、シミュレーションと実機で検証しています。搬送速度27.9〜41.8 mm/sで、平均追従誤差は従来の逆ヤコビアンPI制御の1.1〜1.4 mmから、提案手法の0.3〜0.7 mmへ低減しました。周波数ごとの応答を調べる感度解析から導いた誤差下限とも比較しています。試行数やばらつきはarXivの概要では確認できません。

papers.title: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) augment vision-language-action policies (VLAs) with future prediction so that the policy can anticipate how its actions will affect the physical world. Existing WAMs supervise complete future observations. However, observations typically change little over an action chunk, so the future loss is dominated by copying static background content rather than learning task-relevant robot and object motion, limiting policy learning. Moreover, existing WAMs rely on large video generation models or separate world models, incurring heavy training and inference compute that hinders closed-loop deployment. To improve policy performance, we propose visual residual learning, supervising only the feature change from the current frame to the future frame in a frozen DINOv3 space. Compared with complete future features, this residual learning target yields a higher feature rank with richer and more diverse representations of scene changes, and spatially concentrates on the robot arm and manipulated objects rather than the background. To further improve computational efficiency, we present ResWAM, a residual world-action model with 2.3B parameters in total, including a lightweight 0.5B dual-branch DiT that jointly trains an action branch and a residual branch via conditional flow matching. Without robot pretraining (i.e., pretraining on external robot action trajectories beyond the benchmark demonstrations), ResWAM achieves top average success rates on LIBERO-Plus (81.1%), RoboTwin 2.0 (93.8%), and RoboDojo (9.40% success, 13.41 score) at the lowest training (2.7-4.0 TFLOPs) and inference compute (1.0-1.4 TFLOPs), and leads real-robot Open, Put, and Stack (80.0% average, +10.0% over $π_{0.5}$) at 92.7 ms latency.
papers.headline: 未来の景色全体ではなく「変化」を学び、ロボットの行動予測を効率化するResWAM
papers.summary: 画像と言語から行動を決めるロボット方策に、未来予測を組み込む研究です。未来の画像全体ではなく、現在から変わる特徴だけを学びます。動かない背景の再現に学習が偏るのを抑え、行動と変化を軽量なモデルで同時に学ぶことで、操作の成功率と計算効率の両立を目指します。
papers.advantages: 著者らは、未来全体の特徴を学ぶよりも、特徴の差分を学ぶ方が多様な変化を表現でき、ロボットアームや操作対象に学習を集中できると説明しています。また、大規模な動画生成モデルなどに伴う計算負担の軽減を狙います。実験では、記載された比較で最高の平均成功率と最小の計算量を報告しています。ただし、比較した全手法や条件の詳細はarXivの概要にはありません。
papers.method: 画像の特徴を取り出すDINOv3の重みを固定し、現在と未来のフレームの特徴差分を学習目標にします。背景など変わらない部分を目標から減らすことで、操作に関わる動きを捉えやすくします。全体で23億パラメータのモデルに、行動用と差分用の二つの枝を持つ5億パラメータの拡散Transformerを組み込みます。条件付きフローマッチングという生成学習法で、行動と特徴変化を同時に学びます。
papers.evaluation: ベンチマークの実演データ以外のロボット行動軌跡による事前学習なしで評価しています。成功率はLIBERO-Plusで81.1%、RoboTwin 2.0で93.8%、RoboDojoで9.40%、同スコアは13.41です。計算量は学習時2.7〜4.0 TFLOPs、推論時1.0〜1.4 TFLOPsと報告しています。実機の開く・置く・積む課題では平均成功率80.0%、遅延92.7 msでした。試行数はarXivの概要では確認できません。

papers.title: TMA: Sim-to-Real Forceful Humanoid Manipulation via Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation
papers.abstract: Recent humanoid loco-manipulation in articulated environments has largely focused on geometry-dominant interactions, where success is primarily determined by geometric alignment and motion execution. In contrast, forceful multi-finger manipulation requires the robot to adapt to real-world uncertainties in contact and interaction dynamics. We present Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation (TMA) and an integrated whole-body system for zero-shot sim-to-real forceful humanoid manipulation, and study round-doorknob opening as a challenging benchmark requiring stable multi-finger frictional grasping, sufficient torque generation without slip, force-regulated pushing, and whole-body stability. TMA structures policy learning around interactions observable through tactile feedback, uses cone geometry as an inductive bias for multi-finger contact representation, and adapts motor behavior online from tactile history. An upper-body manipulation policy is trained alongside a pretrained general locomotion controller to coordinate dexterous interaction and whole-body stabilization. Trained entirely in simulation, TMA transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid with BrainCo Revo2 multi-fingered hands and substantially outperforms standard Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA) and reactive tactile policy baselines across four commercial round doorknobs in the real world.
papers.headline: 触覚の履歴で動きを調整し、人型ロボットが丸いドアノブを開けるTMA
papers.summary: 人型ロボットが丸いドアノブを握って回し、押して開ける際に、接触や摩擦の不確かさへ対応する研究です。触覚の履歴から操作動作をその場で調整し、全身の安定化とも組み合わせます。シミュレーションだけで学習し、実機の4種類の市販ドアノブで既存手法を上回ったと報告しています。
papers.advantages: 位置合わせや軌道の実行だけでなく、滑らずに握ることや十分な回転力を出すことなど、力が重要な操作を対象にしています。特徴は、現在の触覚への反応にとどまらず、触覚の履歴から動作を適応させる点です。実機では、標準的なRapid Motor Adaptationという動作適応手法と、反応型の触覚方策を大きく上回ったと報告しています。ただし、改善幅の数値はarXivの概要にはありません。
papers.method: 触覚で観測できる相互作用を中心に操作方策を学習し、触覚の履歴に応じて実行中の動作を調整します。複数の指の接触を表す際には、円錐の幾何形状を学習の手がかりとして組み込みます。ただし、その具体的な表現方法はarXivの概要では確認できません。上半身の操作方策は、事前学習済みの汎用移動制御器と組み合わせて学習し、細かな操作と全身の安定化を連携させます。
papers.evaluation: シミュレーション内だけで学習し、BrainCo Revo2の多指ハンドを備えたUnitree G1へ、実機での追加学習なしに移しています。実環境にある4種類の市販の丸いドアノブを対象に、標準的な動作適応手法と反応型触覚方策を比較しました。課題には、摩擦を使った把持、滑らない回転、力を調整した押し動作、全身の安定が必要です。成功率、試行数、具体的な評価指標はarXivの概要にはありません。

papers.title: RLBench: The Robot Learning Benchmark & Learning Environment
papers.abstract: We present a challenging new benchmark and learning-environment for robot learning: RLBench. The benchmark features 100 completely unique, hand-designed tasks ranging in difficulty, from simple target reaching and door opening, to longer multi-stage tasks, such as opening an oven and placing a tray in it. We provide an array of both proprioceptive observations and visual observations, which include rgb, depth, and segmentation masks from an over-the-shoulder stereo camera and an eye-in-hand monocular camera. Uniquely, each task comes with an infinite supply of demos through the use of motion planners operating on a series of waypoints given during task creation time; enabling an exciting flurry of demonstration-based learning. RLBench has been designed with scalability in mind; new tasks, along with their motion-planned demos, can be easily created and then verified by a series of tools, allowing users to submit their own tasks to the RLBench task repository. This large-scale benchmark aims to accelerate progress in a number of vision-guided manipulation research areas, including: reinforcement learning, imitation learning, multi-task learning, geometric computer vision, and in particular, few-shot learning. With the benchmark's breadth of tasks and demonstrations, we propose the first large-scale few-shot challenge in robotics. We hope that the scale and diversity of RLBench offers unparalleled research opportunities in the robot learning community and beyond.
papers.headline: 100種類の操作課題と自動生成のお手本を備えたロボット学習環境RLBench
papers.summary: ロボットの視覚に基づく操作学習を、幅広い課題で研究するための評価・学習環境RLBenchを提案します。目標への到達から複数段階の操作まで、手作業で設計した100種類の課題を収録。画像やロボット自身の状態に加え、動作計画で継続的に生成できるお手本を提供し、少数の例から学ぶ研究などを支えます。
papers.advantages: 著者が特徴として挙げるのは、課題の多様さ、各課題でお手本を際限なく生成できる仕組み、課題を追加しやすい設計です。また、少数の例から新しい課題を学ぶ「少数例学習」について、ロボティクス初の大規模チャレンジを提案したと主張しています。ただし、既存環境との比較実験や、学習性能の改善を示す数値はarXivの概要にはありません。
papers.method: 課題の作成時に、動作の経由点を指定します。動作計画器がその経由点に沿う動きを計画し、学習用のお手本を生成します。観測には、ロボット自身の状態、カラー画像、奥行き、物体領域を示すマスクを用意します。肩越しのステレオカメラと手先の単眼カメラからの視覚情報も扱います。課題の作成・検証ツールにより、新しい課題とお手本を追加しやすくしています。
papers.evaluation: 評価用の課題群として、目標への到達やドア開けから、オーブンを開けてトレーを入れる複数段階の操作まで、難易度の異なる100種類を用意しています。ただし、これは環境の構成の説明です。どの学習手法を比較したか、どの指標で性能を測ったか、どのような結果が得られたかは、arXivの概要だけでは確認できません。実機実験の実施も記載されていません。

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success
papers.abstract: Recent vision-language-action models (VLAs) build upon pretrained vision-language models and leverage diverse robot datasets to demonstrate strong task execution, language following ability, and semantic generalization. Despite these successes, VLAs struggle with novel robot setups and require fine-tuning to achieve good performance, yet how to most effectively fine-tune them is unclear given many possible strategies. In this work, we study key VLA adaptation design choices such as different action decoding schemes, action representations, and learning objectives for fine-tuning, using OpenVLA as our representative base model. Our empirical analysis informs an Optimized Fine-Tuning (OFT) recipe that integrates parallel decoding, action chunking, a continuous action representation, and a simple L1 regression-based learning objective to altogether improve inference efficiency, policy performance, and flexibility in the model's input-output specifications. We propose OpenVLA-OFT, an instantiation of this recipe, which sets a new state of the art on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, significantly boosting OpenVLA's average success rate across four task suites from 76.5% to 97.1% while increasing action generation throughput by 26$\times$. In real-world evaluations, our fine-tuning recipe enables OpenVLA to successfully execute dexterous, high-frequency control tasks on a bimanual ALOHA robot and outperform other VLAs ($π_0$ and RDT-1B) fine-tuned using their default recipes, as well as strong imitation learning policies trained from scratch (Diffusion Policy and ACT) by up to 15% (absolute) in average success rate. We release code for OFT and pretrained model checkpoints at https://openvla-oft.github.io/.
papers.headline: OpenVLAの追加学習を見直し、動作生成の速度と成功率を改善
papers.summary: 画像と言語からロボットの行動を出力する視覚・言語・行動モデルを、新しいロボット構成に適応させる追加学習を研究します。OpenVLAを対象に、行動の生成方法や表現、学習目標を比較。並列生成や複数時点の行動の一括出力を組み合わせ、シミュレーションと実機で速度や成功率の改善を報告しています。
papers.advantages: 著者は、提案する追加学習法により、推論効率、行動方策の性能、入出力仕様の柔軟性が向上すると主張しています。比較実験では、LIBEROの4課題群でOpenVLAの平均成功率が76.5%から97.1%に上がり、行動生成の処理量が26倍になったと報告しています。柔軟性については、arXivの概要に具体的な評価値はありません。
papers.method: OpenVLAを基礎モデルとして、行動の生成方式、行動の表現、学習目標を調べます。その結果から、行動を並列に生成し、複数時点分をまとめて出力する構成を採用します。行動は連続値で表し、予測値と目標値の絶対誤差を小さくするL1回帰で学習します。この組み合わせをOFTと呼びます。逐次生成を減らす構成で効率を高めますが、各工夫の個別の寄与はarXivの概要では示されていません。
papers.evaluation: LIBEROシミュレーションの4課題群で、平均成功率と行動生成の処理量を評価しています。実機では、双腕ロボットALOHAを使い、器用さと高頻度の制御を要する課題を検証しています。既定の方法で追加学習したπ₀、RDT-1B、および一から学習した模倣学習手法Diffusion Policy、ACTと比べ、平均成功率が最大15パーセントポイント高かったと報告しています。試行数や個別課題の成績は概要にはありません。

papers.title: What Matters in Learning from Offline Human Demonstrations for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Imitating human demonstrations is a promising approach to endow robots with various manipulation capabilities. While recent advances have been made in imitation learning and batch (offline) reinforcement learning, a lack of open-source human datasets and reproducible learning methods make assessing the state of the field difficult. In this paper, we conduct an extensive study of six offline learning algorithms for robot manipulation on five simulated and three real-world multi-stage manipulation tasks of varying complexity, and with datasets of varying quality. Our study analyzes the most critical challenges when learning from offline human data for manipulation. Based on the study, we derive a series of lessons including the sensitivity to different algorithmic design choices, the dependence on the quality of the demonstrations, and the variability based on the stopping criteria due to the different objectives in training and evaluation. We also highlight opportunities for learning from human datasets, such as the ability to learn proficient policies on challenging, multi-stage tasks beyond the scope of current reinforcement learning methods, and the ability to easily scale to natural, real-world manipulation scenarios where only raw sensory signals are available. We have open-sourced our datasets and all algorithm implementations to facilitate future research and fair comparisons in learning from human demonstration data. Codebase, datasets, trained models, and more available at https://arise-initiative.github.io/robomimic-web/
papers.headline: 人のお手本からロボット操作を学ぶ際に、何が性能を左右するかを調査
papers.summary: 事前に集めた人の操作実演だけからロボットを学習させる際に、何が性能を左右するかを調べます。6種類の学習アルゴリズムを、シミュレーション5課題と実世界3課題、品質の異なるデータで検証。手法の設計、実演の品質、学習を止める基準の影響を整理し、再現や比較のためにデータと実装を公開しています。

papers.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
papers.abstract: By transferring knowledge from large, diverse, task-agnostic datasets, modern machine learning models can solve specific downstream tasks either zero-shot or with small task-specific datasets to a high level of performance. While this capability has been demonstrated in other fields such as computer vision, natural language processing or speech recognition, it remains to be shown in robotics, where the generalization capabilities of the models are particularly critical due to the difficulty of collecting real-world robotic data. We argue that one of the keys to the success of such general robotic models lies with open-ended task-agnostic training, combined with high-capacity architectures that can absorb all of the diverse, robotic data. In this paper, we present a model class, dubbed Robotics Transformer, that exhibits promising scalable model properties. We verify our conclusions in a study of different model classes and their ability to generalize as a function of the data size, model size, and data diversity based on a large-scale data collection on real robots performing real-world tasks. The project's website and videos can be found at robotics-transformer1.github.io

papers.title: Event-based Vision: A Survey
papers.abstract: Event cameras are bio-inspired sensors that differ from conventional frame cameras: Instead of capturing images at a fixed rate, they asynchronously measure per-pixel brightness changes, and output a stream of events that encode the time, location and sign of the brightness changes. Event cameras offer attractive properties compared to traditional cameras: high temporal resolution (in the order of microseconds), very high dynamic range (140 dB vs. 60 dB), low power consumption, and high pixel bandwidth (on the order of kHz) resulting in reduced motion blur. Hence, event cameras have a large potential for robotics and computer vision in challenging scenarios for traditional cameras, such as low-latency, high speed, and high dynamic range. However, novel methods are required to process the unconventional output of these sensors in order to unlock their potential. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the emerging field of event-based vision, with a focus on the applications and the algorithms developed to unlock the outstanding properties of event cameras. We present event cameras from their working principle, the actual sensors that are available and the tasks that they have been used for, from low-level vision (feature detection and tracking, optic flow, etc.) to high-level vision (reconstruction, segmentation, recognition). We also discuss the techniques developed to process events, including learning-based techniques, as well as specialized processors for these novel sensors, such as spiking neural networks. Additionally, we highlight the challenges that remain to be tackled and the opportunities that lie ahead in the search for a more efficient, bio-inspired way for machines to perceive and interact with the world.

papers.title: Hindsight Experience Replay
papers.abstract: Dealing with sparse rewards is one of the biggest challenges in Reinforcement Learning (RL). We present a novel technique called Hindsight Experience Replay which allows sample-efficient learning from rewards which are sparse and binary and therefore avoid the need for complicated reward engineering. It can be combined with an arbitrary off-policy RL algorithm and may be seen as a form of implicit curriculum. We demonstrate our approach on the task of manipulating objects with a robotic arm. In particular, we run experiments on three different tasks: pushing, sliding, and pick-and-place, in each case using only binary rewards indicating whether or not the task is completed. Our ablation studies show that Hindsight Experience Replay is a crucial ingredient which makes training possible in these challenging environments. We show that our policies trained on a physics simulation can be deployed on a physical robot and successfully complete the task.

papers.title: Found, but Not Fixed : From Software Vulnerability Discovery to Fixes with Iterative LLM Pipelines
papers.abstract: Software vulnerabilities persist as a critical threat despite the deployment of sophisticated detection tools and AI assistants. While detection has advanced, the subsequent code repair phase remains a primary bottleneck; manual intervention is inherently slow, costly, and prone to introducing secondary regressions and issues. In this paper, we investigate whether an iterative, LLM-based pipeline can provide a robust solution for the automated repair of vulnerable functions in real-world code. We propose a generalized framework that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) through a multi-stage feedback loop. We benchmark this approach against state-of-the-art models, including GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, and Gemini 3 Flash, demonstrating that such a pipeline can achieve high-quality code repair. To support the broader security community, we provide our evaluation framework, fine-tuned weights, and comprehensive experimental dataset on our website: https://sites.google.com/view/llm4cve

papers.title: Set-based State Estimation for Unknown Dynamical Systems from Noisy Output Data with Probabilistic Guarantees
papers.abstract: We develop a methodology for set-based state estimation from noisy input-output trajectories, without a predefined model structure for the unknown state dynamics or access to training state measurements. We derive a bound on the state set diameter that depends on the sensor map and leverage it as a surrogate to formulate a tractable linear program balancing state set tightness against output trajectory coverage. Combining this certificate with deterministic or probabilistically certified measurement noise sets and leveraging the results from scenario optimization with relaxation, we provide joint a posteriori probabilistic guarantees for state inclusion and state set diameter. Numerical simulations corroborate our developed theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
papers.abstract: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. While recent visualization methods have explored distance-based feedback, most are limited to vowels. Extending them to consonants is challenging, as generative embeddings often smooth transient spectral structures. We propose a visualization system for Japanese consonant morae that maps articulatory deviations onto a two-dimensional space defined by temporal and spectral distances from healthy reference speech. Experiments show consistent geometric separation of consonant categories, with Silhouette Coefficients exceeding 0.5 and origin-based ROC-AUC scores above 0.86. Furthermore, evaluations using real dysarthric speech achieved a high ROC-AUC of 0.897 in screening for unclear pronunciations. Perturbation tests confirm orthogonal temporal and spectral shifts, yielding a physically interpretable mapping for rehabilitation.
papers.headline: 日本語の子音を含む拍の発音を、時間と周波数のずれで見える化
papers.summary: 構音障害による発音の変化を、自主的なリハビリで把握しやすくする可視化手法です。日本語のリズムを区切る単位であるモーラに着目し、子音を含む発音と健常な参照音声との違いを、時間と周波数成分の二つの距離で表示します。子音の種類の分離や、不明瞭な発音の識別を実験で評価しています。
papers.advantages: arXivの概要では、従来の距離に基づく可視化の多くは母音に限られ、生成モデルによる表現では子音の短時間の特徴が平滑化されやすいと説明しています。本手法は子音を含むモーラを対象に、時間と周波数成分の違いを解釈しやすい二軸で示します。子音の種類の分離や不明瞭発音の識別結果は報告されていますが、既存手法を上回る比較結果やリハビリ効果は記載されていません。

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.abstract: Training Deep Neural Networks is complicated by the fact that the distribution of each layer's inputs changes during training, as the parameters of the previous layers change. This slows down the training by requiring lower learning rates and careful parameter initialization, and makes it notoriously hard to train models with saturating nonlinearities. We refer to this phenomenon as internal covariate shift, and address the problem by normalizing layer inputs. Our method draws its strength from making normalization a part of the model architecture and performing the normalization for each training mini-batch. Batch Normalization allows us to use much higher learning rates and be less careful about initialization. It also acts as a regularizer, in some cases eliminating the need for Dropout. Applied to a state-of-the-art image classification model, Batch Normalization achieves the same accuracy with 14 times fewer training steps, and beats the original model by a significant margin. Using an ensemble of batch-normalized networks, we improve upon the best published result on ImageNet classification: reaching 4.9% top-5 validation error (and 4.8% test error), exceeding the accuracy of human raters.

papers.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
papers.abstract: Understanding why a model makes a certain prediction can be as crucial as the prediction's accuracy in many applications. However, the highest accuracy for large modern datasets is often achieved by complex models that even experts struggle to interpret, such as ensemble or deep learning models, creating a tension between accuracy and interpretability. In response, various methods have recently been proposed to help users interpret the predictions of complex models, but it is often unclear how these methods are related and when one method is preferable over another. To address this problem, we present a unified framework for interpreting predictions, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations). SHAP assigns each feature an importance value for a particular prediction. Its novel components include: (1) the identification of a new class of additive feature importance measures, and (2) theoretical results showing there is a unique solution in this class with a set of desirable properties. The new class unifies six existing methods, notable because several recent methods in the class lack the proposed desirable properties. Based on insights from this unification, we present new methods that show improved computational performance and/or better consistency with human intuition than previous approaches.
papers.headline: 予測の理由を特徴量の重要度で説明する統一的な枠組みSHAP

papers.title: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge
papers.abstract: The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge is a benchmark in object category classification and detection on hundreds of object categories and millions of images. The challenge has been run annually from 2010 to present, attracting participation from more than fifty institutions. This paper describes the creation of this benchmark dataset and the advances in object recognition that have been possible as a result. We discuss the challenges of collecting large-scale ground truth annotation, highlight key breakthroughs in categorical object recognition, provide a detailed analysis of the current state of the field of large-scale image classification and object detection, and compare the state-of-the-art computer vision accuracy with human accuracy. We conclude with lessons learned in the five years of the challenge, and propose future directions and improvements.

papers.title: DeRep: Learning Depth Representations for End-to-End Navigation in Cluttered Environments
papers.abstract: End-to-end navigation in cluttered environments relies on compact visual representations to support collision avoidance and goal-directed motion. Existing methods typically learn these representations jointly with the policy or through observation reconstruction, which does not explicitly specify what information the representation should preserve. Moreover, they are usually evaluated with a single downstream policy learner, although the benefit of a representation may depend on how the policy is learned. It therefore remains unclear how different representation-learning objectives affect downstream navigation performance and robustness. This work proposes DeRep, a navigation-oriented representation-learning method that combines local bird's-eye-view reachability supervision with depth reconstruction. To compare representation objectives under controlled conditions, we pretrain encoders with a common architecture and freeze them during downstream learning. We evaluate the representations using a linear policy probe, flow-matching imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with PPO. DeRep achieves the lowest linear policy probe prediction error and outperforms reconstruction alone across all six tested PPO conditions. In imitation learning, both reachability-based objectives achieve higher mean success rates than reconstruction alone, with similar mean success rates between the reachability-only and joint objectives. These results demonstrate consistent benefits of incorporating reachability supervision into depth representation pretraining across different downstream learning methods and evaluation conditions. We further deploy the PPO policy with the frozen DeRep encoder in Gazebo and on a physical quadrotor without fine-tuning, demonstrating its capability for zero-shot sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer.
papers.headline: 奥行き表現に「到達できる場所」を学ばせ、障害物の多い環境での移動を支援
papers.summary: 障害物の多い環境で、衝突回避と目的地への移動に役立つ視覚情報を学ぶ研究です。提案手法DeRepは、奥行き画像の復元に加え、周囲のどこへ到達できるかを上から見た局所的な地図で学習します。学習した表現を固定し、異なる行動学習法で比較することで、到達可能性を教える効果を検証しています。

papers.title: Recover, Don't Just Continue: Learning from Feedback for Physical Failure Understanding and Correction
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models are regarded as the cognitive foundation of embodied intelligence, but planning from instructions alone cannot make them reliable. During execution, actions deviate from intended effects, constrained by the embodiment and environment. An embodied brain must understand why execution deviates, identify what can be reliably realized, and revise decisions using interaction experience. These correspond to causal failure localization, capability-constrained adaptation, and experience-driven revision. Current embodied foundation models largely lack these capabilities. To address this, we introduce Embodied-Corrector. We construct failure-recovery data by injecting perturbations at subtask boundaries of successful trajectories, replaying affected subtasks, and keeping failures that are observable from public evidence and recoverable from the current state. We align actions, consequences, failure causes, and recoveries into Judge-Cause-Sub-Fine supervision. Training uses evaluation-first SFT: the model learns Judge and Cause first, then Sub and Fine conditioned on accurate prefixes. Since deployment uses self-generated prefixes, evaluation errors propagate into recovery planning, and response-level rewards are too coarse to locate affected planning tokens. We therefore use OPD to internalize the planning distribution under accurate prefixes into that under self-generated ones: the model generates plans from self-generated prefixes, while a contrastive forward pass with accurate prefixes compares token probabilities to reinforce or suppress planning tokens. At deployment, this branch is removed. Experiments show stronger failure analysis and corrective planning: with a frozen VLA, composite task success improves by 6.1 percentage points; with fixed GPT-5.5 execution, manipulation and navigation tasks improve by 13.9 percentage points.
papers.headline: 実行失敗の原因を理解し、立て直す計画を学ぶEmbodied-Corrector
papers.summary: ロボットなどが指示どおりに動けなかった際、単に作業を続けず、原因を理解して計画を修正する研究です。Embodied-Correctorは、成功した作業に乱れを加えて作った失敗・回復データから学びます。失敗判断や原因分析の誤りが修正計画に伝わる問題にも対処し、実行側のモデルを固定した条件で作業成功率の向上を示しています。

papers.title: BlinkMimic: Training a Humanoid Motion Tracker in Minutes on a Single GPU
papers.abstract: Whole-body motion tracking lets a humanoid robot follow reference motions, but training a tracking policy for a library of motions has usually taken hours of GPU time. SuperMimic showed that the policy can instead be trained by backpropagating through a world model learned from parallel simulation, and InstantTrack added Muon updates, a residual policy around the reference and an averaged deployed policy. We build on both and present BlinkMimic, a recipe that makes this training faster. On a simulated Unitree G1, BlinkMimic trains one policy for all 40 LAFAN1 clips in 3.4 minutes on a single RTX 4090, measured until three consecutive checkpoints reach a normalized return of at least 0.82 with no failed clip (mean of three seeds). We split training time into the cost of an iteration, the iterations needed to fit the motions, and the iterations needed to remove the last failures, and assign each component, inherited or new, to one of these terms. The new components are a step size that decreases once training has progressed, resets directed by failures of the deployed policy under deployment conditions, and GPU graph capture of the whole iteration. A leave-one-out ablation with three seeds per component shows which term each component affects, and further measurements of the gradient, the update rule and the failure cases explain these effects. Code and per-seed results are available at https://github.com/fuyichen0725/blinkmimic.
papers.headline: 人型ロボットの40種類の動作追従を、単一GPUで3.4分で学習
papers.summary: 人型ロボットが手本の全身動作を追う制御方策の学習を、短時間で終える研究です。BlinkMimicは、シミュレーションから学んだ動作予測モデルを使う既存手法を基に、更新幅の調整、失敗に応じたリセット、GPU上の処理の効率化を組み合わせます。シミュレーション上のUnitree G1で、40種類の動作を追う一つの方策を単一GPUで3.4分で学習したと報告しています。
papers.advantages: 著者は、従来は数時間を要した動作追従の学習を高速化する手順を提案しています。SuperMimicの動作予測モデルを通した学習と、InstantTrackの更新方法や手本との差分を出す方策などを引き継ぎ、新たな3要素を加えています。3.4分という結果は明確な到達基準で測定されています。ただし、arXivの概要には既存手法それぞれの所要時間や速度向上倍率はなく、それらとの定量的な差は確認できません。
papers.method: 並列シミュレーションで動作の結果を予測するモデルを学び、そのモデルを通して誤差を逆向きに伝え、手本に追従する方策を更新します。新たな工夫は、学習が進んだ後に更新幅を下げること、運用条件での方策の失敗に基づくリセット、反復処理全体をGPUグラフにまとめることです。学習時間を、1反復の処理時間、動作を覚える反復数、最後の失敗をなくす反復数に分け、各工夫がどこに効くかを整理しています。

papers.title: Solving Rubik's Cube with a Robot Hand
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that models trained only in simulation can be used to solve a manipulation problem of unprecedented complexity on a real robot. This is made possible by two key components: a novel algorithm, which we call automatic domain randomization (ADR) and a robot platform built for machine learning. ADR automatically generates a distribution over randomized environments of ever-increasing difficulty. Control policies and vision state estimators trained with ADR exhibit vastly improved sim2real transfer. For control policies, memory-augmented models trained on an ADR-generated distribution of environments show clear signs of emergent meta-learning at test time. The combination of ADR with our custom robot platform allows us to solve a Rubik's cube with a humanoid robot hand, which involves both control and state estimation problems. Videos summarizing our results are available: https://openai.com/blog/solving-rubiks-cube/

papers.title: End-to-end Driving via Conditional Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Deep networks trained on demonstrations of human driving have learned to follow roads and avoid obstacles. However, driving policies trained via imitation learning cannot be controlled at test time. A vehicle trained end-to-end to imitate an expert cannot be guided to take a specific turn at an upcoming intersection. This limits the utility of such systems. We propose to condition imitation learning on high-level command input. At test time, the learned driving policy functions as a chauffeur that handles sensorimotor coordination but continues to respond to navigational commands. We evaluate different architectures for conditional imitation learning in vision-based driving. We conduct experiments in realistic three-dimensional simulations of urban driving and on a 1/5 scale robotic truck that is trained to drive in a residential area. Both systems drive based on visual input yet remain responsive to high-level navigational commands. The supplementary video can be viewed at https://youtu.be/cFtnflNe5fM

papers.title: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are shown to possess a wealth of actionable knowledge that can be extracted for robot manipulation in the form of reasoning and planning. Despite the progress, most still rely on pre-defined motion primitives to carry out the physical interactions with the environment, which remains a major bottleneck. In this work, we aim to synthesize robot trajectories, i.e., a dense sequence of 6-DoF end-effector waypoints, for a large variety of manipulation tasks given an open-set of instructions and an open-set of objects. We achieve this by first observing that LLMs excel at inferring affordances and constraints given a free-form language instruction. More importantly, by leveraging their code-writing capabilities, they can interact with a vision-language model (VLM) to compose 3D value maps to ground the knowledge into the observation space of the agent. The composed value maps are then used in a model-based planning framework to zero-shot synthesize closed-loop robot trajectories with robustness to dynamic perturbations. We further demonstrate how the proposed framework can benefit from online experiences by efficiently learning a dynamics model for scenes that involve contact-rich interactions. We present a large-scale study of the proposed method in both simulated and real-robot environments, showcasing the ability to perform a large variety of everyday manipulation tasks specified in free-form natural language. Videos and code at https://voxposer.github.io
papers.headline: VoxPoser：言葉の指示を三次元の評価マップに変え、ロボットの動きを計画

papers.title: Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization And Mapping: Towards the Robust-Perception Age
papers.abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM)consists in the concurrent construction of a model of the environment (the map), and the estimation of the state of the robot moving within it. The SLAM community has made astonishing progress over the last 30 years, enabling large-scale real-world applications, and witnessing a steady transition of this technology to industry. We survey the current state of SLAM. We start by presenting what is now the de-facto standard formulation for SLAM. We then review related work, covering a broad set of topics including robustness and scalability in long-term mapping, metric and semantic representations for mapping, theoretical performance guarantees, active SLAM and exploration, and other new frontiers. This paper simultaneously serves as a position paper and tutorial to those who are users of SLAM. By looking at the published research with a critical eye, we delineate open challenges and new research issues, that still deserve careful scientific investigation. The paper also contains the authors' take on two questions that often animate discussions during robotics conferences: Do robots need SLAM? and Is SLAM solved?

papers.title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
papers.abstract: Large language models excel at a wide range of complex tasks. However, enabling general inference in the real world, e.g., for robotics problems, raises the challenge of grounding. We propose embodied language models to directly incorporate real-world continuous sensor modalities into language models and thereby establish the link between words and percepts. Input to our embodied language model are multi-modal sentences that interleave visual, continuous state estimation, and textual input encodings. We train these encodings end-to-end, in conjunction with a pre-trained large language model, for multiple embodied tasks including sequential robotic manipulation planning, visual question answering, and captioning. Our evaluations show that PaLM-E, a single large embodied multimodal model, can address a variety of embodied reasoning tasks, from a variety of observation modalities, on multiple embodiments, and further, exhibits positive transfer: the model benefits from diverse joint training across internet-scale language, vision, and visual-language domains. Our largest model, PaLM-E-562B with 562B parameters, in addition to being trained on robotics tasks, is a visual-language generalist with state-of-the-art performance on OK-VQA, and retains generalist language capabilities with increasing scale.

papers.title: Soft Actor-Critic Algorithms and Applications
papers.abstract: Model-free deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms have been successfully applied to a range of challenging sequential decision making and control tasks. However, these methods typically suffer from two major challenges: high sample complexity and brittleness to hyperparameters. Both of these challenges limit the applicability of such methods to real-world domains. In this paper, we describe Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), our recently introduced off-policy actor-critic algorithm based on the maximum entropy RL framework. In this framework, the actor aims to simultaneously maximize expected return and entropy. That is, to succeed at the task while acting as randomly as possible. We extend SAC to incorporate a number of modifications that accelerate training and improve stability with respect to the hyperparameters, including a constrained formulation that automatically tunes the temperature hyperparameter. We systematically evaluate SAC on a range of benchmark tasks, as well as real-world challenging tasks such as locomotion for a quadrupedal robot and robotic manipulation with a dexterous hand. With these improvements, SAC achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming prior on-policy and off-policy methods in sample-efficiency and asymptotic performance. Furthermore, we demonstrate that, in contrast to other off-policy algorithms, our approach is very stable, achieving similar performance across different random seeds. These results suggest that SAC is a promising candidate for learning in real-world robotics tasks.
papers.headline: SAC：行動の多様性を自動調整し、効率と安定性を高める強化学習
papers.summary: 試行経験の多さと設定値への敏感さが課題となる深層強化学習を改善する研究です。SACは、課題の報酬と行動の多様性を同時に高める学習法です。その釣り合いを自動調整する仕組みなどを加え、学習の効率と安定性を改善します。標準的な評価課題に加え、四足ロボットの移動や器用なロボットハンドの操作でも検証しています。
papers.advantages: 著者は、追加した改良によって学習を速め、設定値に対する安定性を高めると主張しています。比較実験では、従来のオンポリシー手法（現在の行動規則の経験で学ぶ方法）とオフポリシー手法（別の行動規則の経験も使う方法）を、必要な経験量と十分な学習後の性能で上回ったと報告しています。他のオフポリシー手法と比べ、乱数の初期値が異なっても近い性能を得たとしています。
papers.method: SAC（Soft Actor-Critic）は、行動を選ぶ役割と、その行動を評価する役割を組み合わせた強化学習法です。行動選択では、期待される累積報酬とエントロピー（行動のランダムさの尺度）を同時に高めます。課題の達成と多様な行動の両立を狙う仕組みです。両者の釣り合いを決める温度という設定値を、制約付きの定式化で自動調整します。具体的な入力形式や更新手順は概要にありません。
papers.evaluation: 複数の標準的な評価課題と、現実世界の四足ロボットの移動、器用なロボットハンドによる操作を対象に検証しています。従来のオンポリシー・オフポリシー手法と、必要な経験量に対する学習効率と十分な学習後の性能を比較しています。乱数の初期値を変えた際の安定性も評価しています。ただし、課題名、比較手法名、試行回数、具体的な測定値は概要に記載されていません。
papers.futureWork: arXivの概要には今後の課題の記載がありません。著者は、結果からSACを現実世界のロボット学習に有望な候補と位置付けていますが、あらゆる課題での有効性を保証する主張ではありません。追加で確認すべき点は、適用できる課題の範囲、失敗例、実験条件による性能差です。これらは著者が概要で明示した今後の課題ではありません。

papers.title: K2V: Generative Keyframing For Physically Plausible Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video diffusion models are able to generate samples with high-quality appearance and textural qualities. However, content produced by these methods is known to exhibit significant physical errors. This is because, in a classical video generation setting, all physical reasoning must take place simultaneously and exclusively within the diffusion process.We propose to resolve these issues by redistributing the task of physical reasoning onto a language model-backed keyframe generation module, which allows for explicit reasoning in language, and fine-grained control over the appearance of the video at important moments in the video. We then condition a video generation model with these keyframes, reducing the role of the diffusion model to the simpler task of interpolating between physically-correct intermediate states, rather than inferring an entire sequence with diffusion. Results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing approaches, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Physics-IQ Verified benchmark and PhyGenBench.
papers.headline: 重要な場面を先に設計し、物理的な誤りを抑える動画生成
papers.summary: 見た目は高品質でも、物理的に不自然な動きを生む動画生成の問題に取り組む研究です。言語モデルで物理的な整合性を考え、動きの節目となる画像を先に生成します。その画像を条件に動画を作り、動画生成モデルが全体の物理的な動きを一度に推論する負担を減らします。

papers.method: まず、言語モデルを使う生成部が物理的な整合性を推論し、キーフレームと呼ばれる動きの節目の画像を作ります。次に、それらの画像を条件として動画生成モデルへ渡します。動画生成モデルには、物理的に正しい中間状態の間を補う役割を担わせます。全場面の物理的な動きを一度に推論するより、処理を単純化する狙いです。最初に与える入力の形式や、生成画像の物理的な正しさを確認する仕組みは、arXivの概要では不明です。

papers.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
papers.abstract: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. In this work, we introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL), framing SSL as a program search problem and studying how agents navigate this space under limited supervision. We find that even under weak feedback and matched compute, agents can synthesize code that combines and adapts established SSL techniques, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings by up to +21.8%. However, our results identify program selection as a critical bottleneck in AgentSSL, where performance drops by as much as 47% when selecting based on the agent's feedback metric. To systematically study this bottleneck, we introduce ProgramSelectBench, a large-scale benchmark with a combined total of 16,977 agent-generated and human-engineered SSL programs, and evaluate both unsupervised and active program selection methods. We further evaluate AgentSSL on real-world ecology detection tasks, highlighting the opportunities and challenges of transferring agent-discovered strategies beyond controlled benchmarks.
papers.headline: ラベルなしデータを活用するAIエージェント、学習プログラムの選択が課題
papers.summary: 正解ラベルが少なく、ラベルなしデータが多い環境で、機械学習の処理を自動設計する研究です。両方のデータを使う半教師あり学習を、プログラム探索として扱います。AIエージェントが既存手法を組み合わせてコードを作る一方、良いプログラムを選ぶ段階が性能を左右することを示しています。
papers.advantages: 従来の機械学習開発エージェントの研究が、ほぼ正解ラベルのそろった条件に限られていた点に着目しています。本研究は、ラベルが少ない条件で既存の半教師あり学習手法を組み合わせ、調整できるかを調べます。計算資源をそろえ、性能を判断する情報が乏しい条件でも、12設定中8設定で最も強い人手設計の比較手法を上回り、最大＋21.8％の改善を報告しています。ただし、この割合の具体的な算出方法はarXivの概要では不明です。
papers.method: 少数のラベル付きデータと豊富なラベルなしデータを扱う学習方法を、コードとして探索します。エージェントが既存手法を組み合わせ、調整したプログラムを生成し、その中から採用するものを選びます。人手による処理設計の負担を減らす狙いです。ただし、エージェントへ返す評価指標に基づく選択では性能が最大47％低下したと報告されています。生成能力だけでなく、候補の良し悪しを見極める仕組みが重要です。
papers.evaluation: 計算資源をそろえた12設定で、人手設計の強い比較手法と性能を比較しています。さらに、エージェント生成と人手設計を合わせた16,977件の学習プログラムを含むProgramSelectBenchを構築しました。候補選択について、正解情報に頼らない方法と、追加の情報取得を伴う能動的な方法を評価しています。実世界の生態学分野の検出課題でも検証していますが、個別の指標、データの内訳、選択手法や実世界課題の結果はarXivの概要では不明です。

papers.title: BrickFlow: Connectivity-Guided Brick Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Given a set of LEGO parts and an image of an assembled object, our task is to infer the pose of each part to assemble the object. In contrast with traditional 3D reconstruction, doing so requires satisfying discrete physical constraints, which provide structure but render the problem combinatorial and highly sensitive to small pose errors. To learn a prior over how parts fit together, we train a set-conditioned SE(3) flow model on procedurally generated assemblies. We then finetune this model to inject image conditioning, using 1% as much data. However, while the learned flow captures global structure, it does not enforce connectivity. To address this, we introduce an analytic connectivity-field guidance to pull predictions toward connected assemblies at test time. Through this, we demonstrate improved build quality with model size, pretraining, and guidance. We make our models and data available for research purposes at https://kulits.github.io/BrickFlow/
papers.headline: 部品同士の接続を手掛かりに、画像からLEGOの組み立て配置を推定
papers.summary: LEGO部品の集合と完成物の画像から、各部品の位置と向きを推定する研究です。見た目を再現するだけでなく、部品が実際につながる配置を目指します。自動生成した組み立て例で配置を学び、画像に対応するよう追加学習した後、推定時に接続を促す補正を加えます。
papers.advantages: 通常の立体形状の復元とは異なり、部品の組み合わせに関する離散的な物理制約を満たす必要がある課題を扱います。独自の工夫は、学習で得た全体構造の推定に、部品の接続を促す計算上の誘導を加える点です。著者は、モデルの大型化、事前学習、この誘導によって組み立て品質が向上したと報告しています。ただし、既存手法との具体的な比較や、各要素による改善幅はarXivの概要では確認できません。
papers.method: 入力は部品の集合と完成物の画像です。まず、自動生成した組み立て例を使い、部品集合を条件に位置と向きを生成するモデルを学習します。位置と回転をまとめて扱う数学的な表現であるSE(3)上で、配置を変換していく仕組みです。次に、事前学習の1％の量のデータで画像の条件を取り入れる追加学習を行います。最後に、接続状態に基づく解析的な誘導で配置を補正します。全体形状の学習だけでは保証できない接続を促すためです。

papers.title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
papers.abstract: Deep learning frameworks have often focused on either usability or speed, but not both. PyTorch is a machine learning library that shows that these two goals are in fact compatible: it provides an imperative and Pythonic programming style that supports code as a model, makes debugging easy and is consistent with other popular scientific computing libraries, while remaining efficient and supporting hardware accelerators such as GPUs. In this paper, we detail the principles that drove the implementation of PyTorch and how they are reflected in its architecture. We emphasize that every aspect of PyTorch is a regular Python program under the full control of its user. We also explain how the careful and pragmatic implementation of the key components of its runtime enables them to work together to achieve compelling performance. We demonstrate the efficiency of individual subsystems, as well as the overall speed of PyTorch on several common benchmarks.

papers.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
papers.abstract: We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance. Our unified architecture is extremely fast. Our base YOLO model processes images in real-time at 45 frames per second. A smaller version of the network, Fast YOLO, processes an astounding 155 frames per second while still achieving double the mAP of other real-time detectors. Compared to state-of-the-art detection systems, YOLO makes more localization errors but is far less likely to predict false detections where nothing exists. Finally, YOLO learns very general representations of objects. It outperforms all other detection methods, including DPM and R-CNN, by a wide margin when generalizing from natural images to artwork on both the Picasso Dataset and the People-Art Dataset.
papers.headline: YOLO：画像を一度処理するだけで物体の位置と種類を検出
papers.summary: YOLOは、画像内の物体の位置と種類を高速に検出する手法です。画像全体を単一のニューラルネットワークに一度入力し、物体を囲む矩形と種類ごとの確率を直接予測します。検出処理を一体化し、検出性能を目標に全体をまとめて学習できる設計です。

papers.title: Going Deeper with Convolutions
papers.abstract: We propose a deep convolutional neural network architecture codenamed "Inception", which was responsible for setting the new state of the art for classification and detection in the ImageNet Large-Scale Visual Recognition Challenge 2014 (ILSVRC 2014). The main hallmark of this architecture is the improved utilization of the computing resources inside the network. This was achieved by a carefully crafted design that allows for increasing the depth and width of the network while keeping the computational budget constant. To optimize quality, the architectural decisions were based on the Hebbian principle and the intuition of multi-scale processing. One particular incarnation used in our submission for ILSVRC 2014 is called GoogLeNet, a 22 layers deep network, the quality of which is assessed in the context of classification and detection.
papers.headline: Inception：計算量を抑えながら深さと幅を増やす画像認識ネットワーク

papers.title: Reins: Frontier Multimodal Models Driving Real Robot Arms on Long-Horizon Tasks, Zero-Shot
papers.abstract: Frontier models such as GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 can now plan and call tools, yet they still struggle to drive real robots through long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation, blind while the arm moves and while they think. We present Reins, a harness in which an off-the-shelf model operates a dual-arm robot with 3D perception tools and atomic actions that report contact and grip. The model chains actions in one call, each with a condition that must hold, stopping at the first that fails; a second instance, the narrator, watches the cameras continuously and reports what changed with every result. From images, Reins also builds a simulation-ready twin of the scene for continual policy learning. With natural-language prompts and no task-specific code, GPT-6.1 Sol succeeds in 88% of real episodes on five tasks; without the harness, it fails every shell game, taking 8 times as long. Three frontier models perform alike but differ in tracking a scene that changes while the actor thinks. Code will be released upon publication.

papers.title: Embedded Sim-to-Real Visual Servoing: Learned Reaching and Force-Guided Placement
papers.abstract: Embedded perception-to-control systems must combine visual targeting with reliable contact handling under tight computational constraints. We present a shared architecture on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin controlling a Franka Research 3 through Cartesian impedance control. RealSense D435i observations, YOLO11-seg segmentation, depth back-projection, and hand--eye calibration provide metric robot-frame targets. We compare two strategies: compact proximal policy optimization (PPO) policies transferred from simulation for object- and hole-region reaching, and force-guided Cartesian placement using approximately 2 N normal contact and spiral search. The PPO policies achieved 87.2% and 83.1% success over 1000 simulation episodes each. Across 50 real-robot trials per strategy, the learned hybrid and force-guided analytical pipelines achieved 70.0% and 74.0% completion, respectively. Mean perception latency with TensorRT was 34.55 ms. These results support an embedded architecture combining learned free-space reaching with explicit contact correction.

papers.title: DexRemo: A Force-Sensing Hand Platform and Task Suite for Contact-Rich Removal Manipulation
papers.abstract: Many manipulation tasks require separating adhered, embedded, contaminated, or mechanically constrained targets. We study this setting as removal manipulation, where progress depends on evolving contact states that are only partially observable from vision and kinematics. We introduce DexRemo, a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, together with a nine-scenario real-robot task suite spanning adhesive detachment, surface cleaning and self-cleaning, and occluded retrieval. To make multi-finger force observations easier to fuse, we express fingertip forces in a shared wrist-centered frame, giving force components consistent geometric meaning across fingers and time. Using an Action Chunking Transformer backbone, policies fuse multi-view vision, proprioception, fingertip pose, and force observations to predict closed-loop action chunks from demonstrations. Evaluation uses six core benchmark tasks for controlled fingertip-input and force-frame ablations, plus three extension scenarios for additional held-out coverage. Across these evaluations, the learned policies achieve consistent removal performance, and ablations show that wrist-frame forces, especially with fingertip pose, improve stability and generalization over local-frame force inputs and no-force baselines. Project website: https://dexremo.github.io

papers.title: Deep Learning for Detecting Robotic Grasps
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of detecting robotic grasps in an RGB-D view of a scene containing objects. In this work, we apply a deep learning approach to solve this problem, which avoids time-consuming hand-design of features. This presents two main challenges. First, we need to evaluate a huge number of candidate grasps. In order to make detection fast, as well as robust, we present a two-step cascaded structure with two deep networks, where the top detections from the first are re-evaluated by the second. The first network has fewer features, is faster to run, and can effectively prune out unlikely candidate grasps. The second, with more features, is slower but has to run only on the top few detections. Second, we need to handle multimodal inputs well, for which we present a method to apply structured regularization on the weights based on multimodal group regularization. We demonstrate that our method outperforms the previous state-of-the-art methods in robotic grasp detection, and can be used to successfully execute grasps on two different robotic platforms.

papers.title: QT-Opt: Scalable Deep Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Based Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of learning vision-based dynamic manipulation skills using a scalable reinforcement learning approach. We study this problem in the context of grasping, a longstanding challenge in robotic manipulation. In contrast to static learning behaviors that choose a grasp point and then execute the desired grasp, our method enables closed-loop vision-based control, whereby the robot continuously updates its grasp strategy based on the most recent observations to optimize long-horizon grasp success. To that end, we introduce QT-Opt, a scalable self-supervised vision-based reinforcement learning framework that can leverage over 580k real-world grasp attempts to train a deep neural network Q-function with over 1.2M parameters to perform closed-loop, real-world grasping that generalizes to 96% grasp success on unseen objects. Aside from attaining a very high success rate, our method exhibits behaviors that are quite distinct from more standard grasping systems: using only RGB vision-based perception from an over-the-shoulder camera, our method automatically learns regrasping strategies, probes objects to find the most effective grasps, learns to reposition objects and perform other non-prehensile pre-grasp manipulations, and responds dynamically to disturbances and perturbations.

papers.title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
papers.abstract: General-purpose robots need a versatile body and an intelligent mind. Recent advancements in humanoid robots have shown great promise as a hardware platform for building generalist autonomy in the human world. A robot foundation model, trained on massive and diverse data sources, is essential for enabling the robots to reason about novel situations, robustly handle real-world variability, and rapidly learn new tasks. To this end, we introduce GR00T N1, an open foundation model for humanoid robots. GR00T N1 is a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model with a dual-system architecture. The vision-language module (System 2) interprets the environment through vision and language instructions. The subsequent diffusion transformer module (System 1) generates fluid motor actions in real time. Both modules are tightly coupled and jointly trained end-to-end. We train GR00T N1 with a heterogeneous mixture of real-robot trajectories, human videos, and synthetically generated datasets. We show that our generalist robot model GR00T N1 outperforms the state-of-the-art imitation learning baselines on standard simulation benchmarks across multiple robot embodiments. Furthermore, we deploy our model on the Fourier GR-1 humanoid robot for language-conditioned bimanual manipulation tasks, achieving strong performance with high data efficiency.

papers.title: VINS-Mono: A Robust and Versatile Monocular Visual-Inertial State Estimator
papers.abstract: A monocular visual-inertial system (VINS), consisting of a camera and a low-cost inertial measurement unit (IMU), forms the minimum sensor suite for metric six degrees-of-freedom (DOF) state estimation. However, the lack of direct distance measurement poses significant challenges in terms of IMU processing, estimator initialization, extrinsic calibration, and nonlinear optimization. In this work, we present VINS-Mono: a robust and versatile monocular visual-inertial state estimator.Our approach starts with a robust procedure for estimator initialization and failure recovery. A tightly-coupled, nonlinear optimization-based method is used to obtain high accuracy visual-inertial odometry by fusing pre-integrated IMU measurements and feature observations. A loop detection module, in combination with our tightly-coupled formulation, enables relocalization with minimum computation overhead.We additionally perform four degrees-of-freedom pose graph optimization to enforce global consistency. We validate the performance of our system on public datasets and real-world experiments and compare against other state-of-the-art algorithms. We also perform onboard closed-loop autonomous flight on the MAV platform and port the algorithm to an iOS-based demonstration. We highlight that the proposed work is a reliable, complete, and versatile system that is applicable for different applications that require high accuracy localization. We open source our implementations for both PCs and iOS mobile devices.

papers.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
papers.abstract: Large language models can encode a wealth of semantic knowledge about the world. Such knowledge could be extremely useful to robots aiming to act upon high-level, temporally extended instructions expressed in natural language. However, a significant weakness of language models is that they lack real-world experience, which makes it difficult to leverage them for decision making within a given embodiment. For example, asking a language model to describe how to clean a spill might result in a reasonable narrative, but it may not be applicable to a particular agent, such as a robot, that needs to perform this task in a particular environment. We propose to provide real-world grounding by means of pretrained skills, which are used to constrain the model to propose natural language actions that are both feasible and contextually appropriate. The robot can act as the language model's "hands and eyes," while the language model supplies high-level semantic knowledge about the task. We show how low-level skills can be combined with large language models so that the language model provides high-level knowledge about the procedures for performing complex and temporally-extended instructions, while value functions associated with these skills provide the grounding necessary to connect this knowledge to a particular physical environment. We evaluate our method on a number of real-world robotic tasks, where we show the need for real-world grounding and that this approach is capable of completing long-horizon, abstract, natural language instructions on a mobile manipulator. The project's website and the video can be found at https://say-can.github.io/.

papers.title: End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies
papers.abstract: Policy search methods can allow robots to learn control policies for a wide range of tasks, but practical applications of policy search often require hand-engineered components for perception, state estimation, and low-level control. In this paper, we aim to answer the following question: does training the perception and control systems jointly end-to-end provide better performance than training each component separately? To this end, we develop a method that can be used to learn policies that map raw image observations directly to torques at the robot's motors. The policies are represented by deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with 92,000 parameters, and are trained using a partially observed guided policy search method, which transforms policy search into supervised learning, with supervision provided by a simple trajectory-centric reinforcement learning method. We evaluate our method on a range of real-world manipulation tasks that require close coordination between vision and control, such as screwing a cap onto a bottle, and present simulated comparisons to a range of prior policy search methods.

papers.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
papers.abstract: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. In academia, limited compute and inconsistent baselines often restrict evaluations to small-scale, single-point comparisons, making it difficult to establish whether improvements hold at larger scales or translate into broader impact. ArchSpace addresses both gaps as a public platform for Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing Architecture Researc}: each proposal is recorded with its experiments and reasoning, reviewed by the community, and referenced by later work. To evaluate ideas before costly large-scale training, ArchSpace leverages scaling laws to predict model loss at larger scales from smaller experiments, a practice widely adopted in industry. We provide initial references that make the platform usable: Qwen3.5 and OLMo3 baselines, fitted scaling laws, and a reusable training recipe. Ideas validated through this review can in turn become new baselines, and ArchSpace thereby aims to broaden the range of ideas that shape the next generation of models.

papers.title: ProtoVis-Nav: Prototypical Visual Imagination for Visual-Spatial Aligned UAV Navigation
papers.abstract: Vision language navigation (VLN) is very challenging for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) since small errors in 3D motion prediction can lead to navigation errors and collisions. Unable to fathom execution outcomes in 3D environments, existing methods often struggle to predict accurate navigation waypoints from language instructions. To solve this, we introduce the Prototypical Visual Imagination framework, shortened as ProtoVis-Nav, which forces the model to imagine an outcome-associated local visual representation for the intended next UAV movement. Specifically, we predict feature prototypes and use their linear combination to estimate the visual feature of the target region. In this manner, the VLN model first imagines the local visual representation of the next intended location, and then uses predicted prototypes as context for generating the final action, promoting alignment between visual context and waypoint outputs. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the ProtoVis-Nav framework and show substantial improvements over existing baselines.
papers.headline: 次の移動先の見え方を予測し、ドローンの言語指示による航法を支援

papers.title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
papers.abstract: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. Existing neurosymbolic methods such as Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) offer constraint-satisfying reinforcement learning (RL) via differentiable symbolic supervision but assume a finite, discrete action space. We present a PLPG-inspired continuous allocation method that estimates the probability that the policy's own executed action satisfies the investment mandate, using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling, and adds it to the training objective. No post-hoc enforcement mechanism intercepts actions at inference time and compliance is learned by the agent. Audited directly on deterministic mean actions with no correction, the policy reduces violations of a six-rule regime-conditional mandate from 96-98% for unconstrained RL and 33.4% for a reward-penalty baseline to 4.8%, showing that a continuous-action neurosymbolic policy can substantially internalize a symbolic mandate.
papers.headline: 投資ルールを学習に組み込み、資産配分の違反率を4.8％に低減
papers.summary: 機関投資家の資産配分では、市場状況に応じた投資ルールを守る必要があります。本研究は、連続的な配分を出す強化学習に、行動がルールを満たす確率を組み込みます。出力後に配分を修正せず、学習によって違反を減らす方法で、６つのルールに対する違反率4.8％を報告しています。
papers.advantages: 論理ルールによる指導を強化学習に取り込む既存手法PLPGは、有限個の離散的な行動を前提とします。本研究は、その考え方を連続的な資産配分に応用しています。出力後の強制修正ではなく、方策自体にルール順守を学ばせる点が特徴です。比較では、違反率が制約なしの強化学習の96〜98％、報酬に罰則を加える手法の33.4％に対し、4.8％でした。ただし、完全な順守ではありません。
papers.method: 学習した行動選択規則を「方策」と呼びます。本手法は、方策が実際に出す配分が投資ルールを満たす確率を、複数の乱数サンプルで推定します。その際、乱数を使う計算でも学習に必要な勾配を伝えられる再パラメータ化を用い、順守確率を学習目的に加えます。ルールに沿う配分を方策自身が選ぶよう促す仕組みです。運用時に出力を差し止めたり、修正したりする機構は使いません。
papers.evaluation: 市場状況に応じて条件が変わる６つの投資ルールについて評価しています。行動の分布から平均値を取り、毎回同じ配分を出す設定で、補正せずに直接順守を点検しました。違反率は提案手法が4.8％で、制約なしの強化学習と報酬罰則方式を下回りました。arXivの概要には、対象資産、市場データ、評価期間、違反率の集計単位、収益性の比較結果は記載されていません。
papers.futureWork: arXivの概要には今後の課題の記載がありません。報告された違反率は4.8％で、ルール違反が残っています。ただし、その解消を今後の課題として掲げているとは記載されていません。追加で確認すべき点は、残る違反の内容、別の投資ルールや市場状況での順守率、収益性との両立です。これらは著者が明示した研究計画ではありません。

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.abstract: While the Transformer architecture has become the de-facto standard for natural language processing tasks, its applications to computer vision remain limited. In vision, attention is either applied in conjunction with convolutional networks, or used to replace certain components of convolutional networks while keeping their overall structure in place. We show that this reliance on CNNs is not necessary and a pure transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches can perform very well on image classification tasks. When pre-trained on large amounts of data and transferred to multiple mid-sized or small image recognition benchmarks (ImageNet, CIFAR-100, VTAB, etc.), Vision Transformer (ViT) attains excellent results compared to state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources to train.
papers.headline: 画像を小さな領域の列として扱うVision Transformer
papers.summary: 画像分類で、畳み込みニューラルネットワーク（CNN）に頼らない構成を検討した研究です。画像を小さな領域に分け、その列をTransformerという要素間の関係を学ぶモデルに直接入力します。大量のデータで事前学習し、複数の画像認識課題へ応用することで、高い性能と学習時の計算資源削減を報告しています。

papers.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
papers.abstract: Tree boosting is a highly effective and widely used machine learning method. In this paper, we describe a scalable end-to-end tree boosting system called XGBoost, which is used widely by data scientists to achieve state-of-the-art results on many machine learning challenges. We propose a novel sparsity-aware algorithm for sparse data and weighted quantile sketch for approximate tree learning. More importantly, we provide insights on cache access patterns, data compression and sharding to build a scalable tree boosting system. By combining these insights, XGBoost scales beyond billions of examples using far fewer resources than existing systems.
papers.headline: 疎なデータへの対応と計算効率を追求するXGBoost

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art computer vision systems are trained to predict a fixed set of predetermined object categories. This restricted form of supervision limits their generality and usability since additional labeled data is needed to specify any other visual concept. Learning directly from raw text about images is a promising alternative which leverages a much broader source of supervision. We demonstrate that the simple pre-training task of predicting which caption goes with which image is an efficient and scalable way to learn SOTA image representations from scratch on a dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet. After pre-training, natural language is used to reference learned visual concepts (or describe new ones) enabling zero-shot transfer of the model to downstream tasks. We study the performance of this approach by benchmarking on over 30 different existing computer vision datasets, spanning tasks such as OCR, action recognition in videos, geo-localization, and many types of fine-grained object classification. The model transfers non-trivially to most tasks and is often competitive with a fully supervised baseline without the need for any dataset specific training. For instance, we match the accuracy of the original ResNet-50 on ImageNet zero-shot without needing to use any of the 1.28 million training examples it was trained on. We release our code and pre-trained model weights at https://github.com/OpenAI/CLIP.
papers.headline: 画像と文章の対応から学び、追加学習なしで画像認識へ応用するCLIP
papers.summary: あらかじめ決めた分類項目への依存を減らすため、画像と説明文の対応から視覚的な特徴を学ぶ研究です。インターネット由来の4億組の画像・文章で事前学習し、認識したい概念を自然言語で指定します。課題ごとの追加学習をしない「ゼロショット転移」を評価し、多様な画像認識課題への応用を報告しています。
papers.advantages: 固定された分類項目のラベルに代えて、画像に関する文章を学習の手がかりにする点が特徴です。著者は、これにより幅広い視覚概念を扱えるとしています。比較結果として、多くの課題で、課題別の追加学習なしでも、正解ラベルで学習した比較モデルにしばしば匹敵すると報告しています。ImageNetでは、元のResNet-50という画像認識モデルと同等の精度を、同データセットで学習せずに達成したと述べています。
papers.method: 4億組の画像と文章を入力し、どの説明文がどの画像に対応するかを予測する課題で事前学習します。画像と文章の対応を手がかりにすることで、固定の分類項目だけに縛られない視覚的な特徴の獲得を目指します。事前学習後は、認識したい概念を自然言語で指定し、課題別の追加学習なしで認識へ応用します。具体的なネットワーク構造や、対応を予測する計算式は、arXivの概要には記載されていません。
papers.evaluation: 文字読み取り、動画の動作認識、地理的位置の推定、細かな種類の物体分類など、30を超える既存の視覚データセットで評価しています。課題別に正解ラベルを使って学習したモデルと比較し、追加学習なしでもしばしば競争力があると報告しています。ImageNetでは、ResNet-50が学習に用いた128万件を使わずに同等の精度を達成したとしています。具体的な精度の値や課題別の結果は記載されていません。

papers.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
papers.abstract: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO). By leveraging group reward distributions, TGRPO effectively reinforces high-reward action sequences. Evaluated on 273 held-out UAV-Flow-Sim episodes, pretrained FlowVLA achieves a mean success rate of 75.58%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.72 percentage points, which TGRPO post-training further elevates to 93.16% with superior sample efficiency. Physical UAV experiments demonstrate robust execution of object-relative commands in both indoor and outdoor real-world scenes. Together, Flow establishes a novel benchmark and learning framework for language-conditioned flight maneuvers.
papers.headline: 短い言葉でドローンを動かす、物体との位置関係に基づく飛行学習
papers.summary: 短い自然言語の指示に従い、物体との位置関係を踏まえてドローンを操縦する研究です。機体視点の画像と現在の運動状態から、連続的な飛行操作を生成します。実世界とシミュレーションの飛行データ、評価環境、学習手法を整備し、長距離の経路計画に比べて研究が少なかった近距離の飛行操作を扱います。
papers.advantages: 著者は、基本的な移動から物体に関わる複雑な操作までを扱う、共通の学習・評価基盤を提案しています。比較実験では、事前学習したFlowVLAの平均成功率が最も強い比較手法を6.72ポイント上回りました。追加学習による成功率向上と優れたサンプル効率も報告されています。ただし、比較手法の名前やサンプル効率の具体的な差は、arXivの概要には記載されていません。
papers.method: 言語指示、機体視点の画像、現在の運動状態を入力し、FlowVLAが連続的な飛行操作を出力します。まず実世界とシミュレーションの操縦例を混ぜ、手本の操作をまねる模倣学習を行います。その後、オンラインで追加学習するTGRPOを適用します。TGRPOは複数の行動列から得られる報酬の分布を利用し、高い報酬を得た行動列を重点的に強化する仕組みです。

papers.title: Inner Product Regularization for Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Robots that learn from demonstrations should extrapolate their policy despite state perturbations such as sensor noise, scene variation, and compounding errors. One approach to this robustness is regularization. Prior regularizers consider each state on its own and limit how sensitive the policy is to any perturbation at that state. By contrast, we explore how the policy's output shifts when given the same perturbation at different states. Our insight is that, locally, the robot should respond to state perturbations in a consistent manner: e.g., if changing an irrelevant object position does not impact the policy at one state, that same change should not shift the policy output at a nearby state. Applying this insight, we develop inner product regularization (InneR). We show that the inner product on action space induces an inner product on state space through the policy Jacobian (the Fisher information for stochastic policies), and that the null space of this inner product governs which state perturbations have a first-order effect on the policy. By clustering states whose inner products are aligned, averaging the inner products within each cluster, and minimizing the smallest eigenvalues of that average, InneR shapes the learned policy so that nearby states share a common null space. InneR enforces consistent responses to perturbations without limiting policy expressiveness, and can be appended to existing imitation learning pipelines for deterministic or stochastic policies. In simulated experiments, InneR makes learned policies more robust to irrelevant state dimensions and shifts between training and test distributions, whereas norm penalties often perform worse than behavior cloning. On a real robot arm performing three manipulation tasks, InneR raises the average success rate of a diffusion policy from 18% to 57% without additional data.
papers.headline: 状態の変化への反応をそろえ、模倣学習ロボットの頑健性を高める
papers.summary: 手本から動作を学ぶロボットが、センサー雑音や場面の変化で失敗しにくくなるようにする研究です。各状態で出力の変化を抑えるだけでなく、近い状態同士で同じ変化に一貫して反応するよう学習を調整します。提案手法InneRは、動作に無関係な状態の変化を共通して無視できる方策を目指します。
papers.advantages: 従来の正則化が各状態での変化への敏感さを個別に抑えるのに対し、InneRは状態間で反応をそろえます。著者は、行動を決める方策の表現力を制限せず、確定的・確率的な既存の模倣学習に追加できると主張しています。実験では、シミュレーションで頑健性が向上し、実機では追加データなしで平均成功率が18%から57%に上がったと報告されています。
papers.method: 方策の出力が状態の微小変化にどう反応するかを、ヤコビ行列という局所的な変化率で表します。これを用い、状態の変化同士の関係を測る内積を構成します。その内積が似た状態をまとめ、各群の内積を平均して小さい固有値を最小化します。これにより、出力に一次の影響を与えない変化の方向を近い状態間で共通化し、無関係な変化への一貫した反応を促します。
papers.evaluation: シミュレーションでは、動作に無関係な状態成分と、学習時・評価時のデータ分布の違いに対する頑健性を検証しています。変化の大きさを抑えるノルム罰則は、手本の行動を直接まねる行動クローニングより悪い場合が多かったと報告されています。実機のロボットアームでは3種類の操作課題を実施し、ノイズ除去を利用して行動を生成する拡散方策の平均成功率が18%から57%に向上しました。試行数や課題名は記載されていません。

papers.title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems. Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation. This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation. We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.
